words.gloss: book (of — مُضَاف, no الـ or tanwīn of its own)
brother (of — one of the five nouns, جَرّ marked by ي instead of kasra; itself مُضَاف to الطَّالِبِ)
the student (مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ of أَخِي — genitive)

en: I saw the teachers at school.

words.gloss: the teachers (sound masculine plural, نَصْب marked by ـِينَ, not the ـُونَ of رَفْع)

en: I saw the [female] teachers at school.

words.gloss: the [female] teachers (sound feminine plural, نَصْب unexpectedly marked by kasra ـِ, identical to its own جَرّ form)
these (non-human plural takes the feminine-singular demonstrative)
offices (plural of مَكْتَب — a diptote broken-plural pattern; رَفْع marked by ḍamma, no tanwīn)
new (feminine-singular agreement, matching the non-human plural)
offices (diptote; نَصْب marked by fatḥa, no tanwīn)
house (of — مُضَاف, no الـ or tanwīn of its own)
friends (plural of صَدِيق — a diptote plural pattern; INDEFINITE, so جَرّ is marked by fatḥa, not kasra)
the friends (same diptote plural, now DEFINITE with الـ — جَرّ returns to the regular kasra)

vowelled: هُوَ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ
translit: huwa yurīdu an yadhhaba ilā al-madrasati
en: He wants to go to school.

words.gloss: wants (present tense, مَرْفُوع — the default, no trigger before it)
to (subordinates the next verb, triggering مَنْصُوب)
go (مَنْصُوب — fatḥa instead of the usual ḍamma, triggered by أَنْ)

audio: هُوَ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ

en: He will never go to school.

words.gloss: will never (negates the future, triggering مَنْصُوب)
go (مَنْصُوب — fatḥa instead of ḍamma, triggered by لَنْ)

en: He did not go to school.

words.gloss: did not (negates the PAST, triggering مَجْزُوم on the present-tense verb after it)
go (مَجْزُوم — sukūn, no ending vowel at all, triggered by لَمْ)
happy (الْحَال — describes the man's state WHILE returning, accusative and indefinite)
sad (الْحَال — describes the student's state WHILE coming, accusative and indefinite)
in the morning (مَفْعُول فِيهِ — ظَرْف زَمَان, accusative, implying "في" with no preposition written)
at night (مَفْعُول فِيهِ — ظَرْف زَمَان, accusative)

en: I traveled along with a friend.

words.gloss: along with (وَاو الْمَعِيَّة — accompaniment, not the plain conjunction "and")
a friend (مَفْعُول مَعَهُ — accusative, did not itself take part in the traveling)

en: The man sat along with his son.

words.gloss: his son (مَفْعُول مَعَهُ — accusative; the fatḥa before the attached pronoun هُ shows the case)
big (النَّعْت — agrees with الْبَيْتُ in definiteness, gender, number, AND case)
tall (النَّعْت — matches الرَّجُلَ's definiteness, gender, number, and accusative case)

en: The father and the mother are happy.

words.gloss: the father (الْمَعْطُوف عَلَيْه — the noun conjoined TO, رَفْع)
the mother (الْمَعْطُوف — takes the SAME case, رَفْع, as الْأَبُ)
happy (dual predicate, agreeing with the combined pair)

en: I read the book and the lesson.

words.gloss: the book (الْمَعْطُوف عَلَيْه — نَصْب, مَفْعُول بِهِ)
the lesson (الْمَعْطُوف — takes the SAME case, نَصْب, as الْكِتَابَ)
work (الْمَفْعُول الْمُطْلَق — a مَصْدَر of عَمِلَ itself, accusative)
good (its نَعْت — agrees in case, accusative)

vowelled: أَغْلَقَ الرَّجُلُ النَّافِذَةَ خَوْفًا مِنَ الرِّيحِ
translit: aghlaqa ar-rajulu an-nāfidhata khawfan mina ar-rīḥi
en: The man closed the window out of fear of the wind.

words.gloss: out of fear (الْمَفْعُول لِأَجْلِه — an indefinite مَصْدَر, accusative, answering "why?")

audio: أَغْلَقَ الرَّجُلُ النَّافِذَةَ خَوْفًا مِنَ الرِّيحِ

vowelled: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ — وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ — مَا اسْمُكَ؟ — اسْمِي سَمِيرٌ، وَأَنَا مُعَلِّمٌ. وَأَنْتَ؟ — أَنَا دَانِيَال، وَأَنَا طَالِبٌ.
translit: as-salāmu ʿalaykum — wa-ʿalaykumu s-salāmu wa-raḥmatu llāhi — mā smuka? — ismī samīrun, wa-anā muʿallimun. wa-anta? — anā dāniyāl, wa-anā ṭālibun.
en: — Peace be upon you. — And upon you be peace and Allah's mercy. — What is your name? — My name is Samir, and I am a teacher. And you? — I am Daniel, and I am a student.

turns.en: And upon you be peace and Allah's mercy.
My name is Samir, and I am a teacher. And you?
I am Daniel, and I am a student.

vowelled: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَا أَخِي — وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ — هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ؟ — نَعَمْ، أَنَا ذَاهِبٌ لِلصَّلَاةِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ — أَنَا قَادِمٌ مَعَكَ
translit: as-salāmu ʿalaykum yā akhī — wa-ʿalaykumu s-salāmu wa-raḥmatu llāhi wa-barakātuhu — hal anta dhāhibun ilā l-masjidi? — naʿam, anā dhāhibun li-ṣ-ṣalāti in shāʾa llāhu — anā qādimun maʿaka
en: — Peace be upon you, my brother. — And upon you be peace, and Allah's mercy and blessings. — Are you going to the mosque? — Yes, I am going for the prayer, God willing. — I am coming with you.

turns.en: Peace be upon you, my brother.
And upon you be peace, and Allah's mercy and blessings.
Are you going to the mosque?

turns.translit: naʿam, anā dhāhibun li-ṣ-ṣalāti in shāʾa llāhu
turns.en: Yes, I am going for the prayer, God willing.
